beats: A kid taps a button, waiting for the app to read it aloud — and nothing comes out.
Every spoken line had been a separate pre-recorded clip; anything missing one just stayed silent.
The app's wrapper had no way to generate speech on its own, the way a browser normally would.
Now it borrows the phone's own text-to-speech voice whenever nothing was pre-recorded.
Cached or not, every phrase gets read out loud now.
